newsitem.title: USA: Panenergy says 700 mmcfd gas shut in USG.
newsitem.headline: Panenergy says 700 mmcfd gas shut in USG.

text.p: Panenergy Corp said Monday producers in the U.S. Gulf have shut in about 700 million cubic feet a day (mmcfd) of natural gas production as a preacaution against tropical storm Josephine.
"On Texas Eastern, there's about 350 million (cfd) shut in because of Josephine, and the Terrebonne system on Trunkline lost about 350 million," a company spokesman said.
He said most of the gas lost on Texas Eastern was on the Venice system off eastern Louisiana.
"We're not sure when it will be back. The feeling is there will be more production turned off as a precaution," he said.
He said the company was working with shippers to locate alternative sources of supply.
At 0500 EDT, Josephine, with winds of about 50 mph, was 340 miles southwest of Apalachicola, Florida, and was moving east-northeast at 15 mph.
